feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: clear positioning, relevant scope, and solid evidence of progression and ownership. It reads professionally and is largely polished, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by emphasizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior brand: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility signals: named employer, long tenure, promotion history, and concrete scale metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”  
- Broad, relevant capability mix: strategy, governance, analytics, CMS/platform work, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are well aligned to modern digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Increase impact language: several bullets describe duties (“support,” “advise,” “develop”) rather than business/user outcomes; add results such as efficiency gains, engagement lifts, adoption, or cost savings where possible.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” mixed punctuation in lists, and slightly awkward phrasing in “Ranked among the top public universities…” Also consider whether “Coleman DAVIS” should use normal title case unless intentional. No obvious misspellings; grammar is generally strong.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several competency areas listed elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace the second sentence with a more outcome-oriented summary tied to recent work: “Leads enterprise web modernization, digital governance, analytics and AI-enabled content experiences for complex public-sector organizations.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience to increase impact, e.g., “including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views.”
- Tighten “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications” to “building the platforms and operating models that power high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Consider revised version: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms and operating models that power high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, digital governance, analytics infrastructure and AI-enabled content experiences for mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial systems,” “multimedia production,” and “analytics infrastructure” are already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Recent Projects; keep the intro broader unless adding a specific proof point.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization”; “Digital governance and editorial operations” instead of “editorial systems.”
- Prioritize the most marketable, recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, workflow automation, and public-sector communications.
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- If space is tight, drop “Multi-channel communications operations,” which is broad and better evidenced elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with the header, recent project, and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already covered in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce your current positioning, but the block is too dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a short, punchy accomplishment rather than a full sentence.
- Tighten wording: “AI-powered” is clearer than “AI-enabled,” and “10 x 20-foot” is more consistent stylistically than “10×20-foot.”
- Emphasize outcomes or scope where possible: e.g., “improve policy-content discovery,” “support ongoing campaign expansion,” “integrated with the main website.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI-Powered Hybrid Search — Built a legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat. We Are Counties Microsite — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and reusable modular components. Organization Anniversary Campaign — Created a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series — Produced an ongoing advocacy video program across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search, microsites, and advocacy video closely overlap with current and prior roles; keep this block concise to avoid repeating Work Experience verbatim.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground the highest-impact themes: enterprise web modernization, Drupal campaign delivery, and AI-enabled search.

Suggested edit:
- Open with outcome + scope: “Lead digital strategy, content operations, and enterprise web improvement for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one stronger line: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordinated communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS work more results-oriented: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits; provided front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Keep the AI work as a distinct capstone bullet: “Lead an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user-facing discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic “governance,” “analytics,” and “multi-channel communications” language already used heavily in the NACo roles.
- The footer project examples already cover microsites and AI search, so this item should stay higher-level unless you add measurable outcomes.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization as the signature achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-driven: add growth, engagement, deliverability, production volume, or campaign impact if available; otherwise shorten.
- Combine governance/analytics bullets for concision: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery while formalizing publishing standards and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video leadership also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the in-house studio, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling NACo’s editorial planning and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-led: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very similar to the Director role; avoid repeating channel lists.
- Weekly video/update language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project section.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing leadership scope and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy and platform governance
- Editorial operations, publishing standards, and content systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership for web, email, social, and video
- Public-sector stakeholder engagement and advocacy communications
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations and editorial planning” to sound more senior and align with recent leadership roles.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixed styles like “messaging” vs. “planning” vs. “leadership.”
- If space allows, add one scale cue in the section title or nearby summary instead of here, since impact is already evidenced in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution strengths rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters tied to recent work: “Drupal platform delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older items unless job-relevant: remove jQuery first; keep SharePoint/Power Pages only if the target role explicitly asks for Microsoft ecosystem experience.
- Use stronger phrasing: replace “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” with “Web Platform Delivery & Technical Implementation” or “CMS Platforms, Integrations & AI Search.”
- If space allows, add one proof point in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., Drupal migration for a 10,000+ page site or AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost line-for-line.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcomes-oriented: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI & Looker Studio reporting” is stronger than listing each tool separately.
- Replace generic terms with sharper phrasing: use “Executive KPI dashboards” instead of “Leadership reporting.”
- Clarify optimization scope: change “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and content performance optimization.”
- Suggested version: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and reporting • SEO, UX and content performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the full tool list elsewhere; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave exhaustive platforms to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems

- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo bullets. Make it more specific to senior-level delivery and systems ownership, not just task execution.

Suggested edit:

- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production

- “Livestreaming” duplicates “livestream operations” in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “event delivery” in the title; avoid repeating both terms too closely

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. In a recent, impact-led CV, this item should either add specificity or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Web Platforms & CMS Administration
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise, Drupal 10) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If accurate, add level/scope instead of more tools: Drupal site building, content architecture, publishing workflows, microsites
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; lead with Drupal given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider deleting one version or making this one more implementation-focused
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the rest unless it supported a notable project or deployment workflow

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and calibrated to the senior, recent work shown elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied capability: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Deployment.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context in brief: “for Drupal-based public websites, campaign microsites, analytics tagging, and deployment workflows.”
- Consider replacing older/generic terms with stronger specifics where possible, e.g., “serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers)” or “CI/CD workflows (GitHub Actions).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- If space is tight, keep this section more tool-specific and let Topline Skills carry the broader summary.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped systems: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most differentiating tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira.
- If true, add a light outcome-oriented label: “Used to build editorial planning systems, automate handoffs/notifications, and support cross-team publishing operations.”
- Consider dropping one or two generic collaboration tools if space is tight; Slack and Teams add less value than automation/project systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them verbatim without added context.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar signals; listing all four may feel redundant unless tailored by relevance.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Given the CV’s strong email/communications leadership, this item should signal enterprise email and member engagement capability more clearly.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/context: Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and member communications
- Best option: fold one capability phrase into the line, e.g. Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | email automation, segmentation, newsletter operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you add a distinct capability angle.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item platform-specific rather than broad.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is mostly a keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analytics infrastructure and optimization methods most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO/performance analysis • A/B testing • Executive dashboarding
- Put the strongest, most recent enterprise tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “Executive dashboarding” or “KPI reporting” to sound more outcome-oriented and less generic.
- If space allows elsewhere, quantify impact in experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “analytics stack supporting 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider trimming one version or making this one tools-only.
- “SEO” also overlaps with broader digital strategy language; “SEO/performance analysis” is more specific.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, production, and platform support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, livestream frequency, weekly video cadence, audience reach, or number of campaigns/events supported.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce soft language: replace “high-impact digital content” with named deliverables like “livestreamed events, weekly advocacy video updates, and multimedia web content.”
- Clarify supervision level: “provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate” could become “coordinated daily work of 1 digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching or establishing the format, not expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” risks repeating later governance/operations bullets; keep this version tactical and foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast as a first.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Add the clearest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” to something more active, e.g. “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audiences served, or types of research/projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad digital production language already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia here; podcast launch is the more distinctive accomplishment.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
